messages.content: Can you analyze the DNA sequence "AGCTTAGCTA" and "AGCTTAGGCTA" using the reference sequence "AGCTTAGCTA" to identify any potential 'insertion' mutations, then repeat the same analysis for 'deletion' and 'substitution' mutations?

function.name: analyze_dna_sequence
function.description: Analyzes the DNA sequence based on a reference sequence and return any potential mutations. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sequence.description: The DNA sequence to be analyzed.

mutation_type.description: Type of the mutation to be looked for in the sequence.

message.reasoning: The user wants to analyze two sequences against a reference. They want insertion analysis first, then deletion, then substitution. We need to call the function three times, each with mutation_type set accordingly. The function signature: analyze_dna_sequence takes sequence, reference_sequence, mutation_type optional default insertion. So we can call with mutation_type "insertion" for first, "deletion" second, "substitution" third. The user provided two sequences: "AGCTTAGCTA" and "AGCTTAGGCTA". The reference is "AGCTTAGCTA". So we need to analyze each sequence separately? The user says "analyze the DNA sequence 'AGCTTAGCTA' and 'AGCTTAGGCTA' using the reference sequence 'AGCTTAGCTA' to identify any potential 'insertion' mutations, then repeat the same analysis for 'deletion' and 'substitution' mutations?" That implies we need to analyze both sequences for each mutation type. So we need to call the function twice per mutation type. So total six calls. But the function only accepts one sequence at a time. So we need to call it for each sequence. So we will call analyze_dna_sequence for sequence "AGCTTAGCTA" with reference "AGCTTAGCTA" and mutation_type "insertion". Then for sequence "AGCTTAGGCTA" with same reference and mutation_type "insertion". Then repeat for deletion and substitution. So six calls. We'll produce calls in order.
